title: Buttermilk Biscuits
source: Handwritten notes; method from Alton Brown, Food Network

items.body: Preheat the oven to 400 °F (204 °C). Keep the butter and buttermilk in the fridge until you need them.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together in a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.

Make a well in the middle and pour in the buttermilk. Stir until the dough just comes together, then knead it in the bowl until all the flour is taken up. If it’s still dry, add up to 15 g more buttermilk.
Turn the dough out onto a floured counter. Fold it over and knead gently for 30 s, until soft and smooth. Press it into a rectangle 1 in thick.
Cut into 12 squares with the bench scraper, pushing straight down without twisting. Set them on the sheet pan so they just touch. Press a thumb dimple into the center of each.
Bake until tall and light gold on top, 15–20 min.

nutritionSource: USDA SR Legacy (butter, buttermilk) and labels (King Arthur all-purpose, Davis, Morton). Counter flour not counted.
notes: Half batch, from the second column of the notes: 180 g flour, ½ tsp salt, 1½ tsp baking powder, 43 g butter, 120 g buttermilk. Makes 6.

Alton’s version: 340 g flour, 4 tsp baking powder, ¼ tsp baking soda, ¾ tsp kosher salt, 1 oz butter + 2 oz shortening, 8 fl oz buttermilk, cut in 3 in rounds. Squares here since there’s no biscuit cutter.
